what: Antero Midstream owns the pipelines, compressors and water systems that gather natural gas from Antero Resources' Appalachian wells and move it to the interstate pipelines.
customers: Antero Resources, which provides essentially all the volumes under long-term contracts.
money: pipelines and compressors collecting gas from wellheads
fresh water delivery and produced water disposal for drilling
moat: Infrastructure physically connected to a specific producer's wells under long-term contracts with minimum volume commitments. Nobody else can serve those wells.
risks: One customer provides nearly all revenue, so Antero Resources' drilling plans decide everything
Free cash flow of only $62M because gathering expansion consumes capital
opportunities: A 34.7% net margin, the economics of a toll road
Revenue grew steadily from $898M to $1.2B in four years
Analysts see about 17% upside, and contracts carry minimum volume commitments regardless of gas prices
watch: Antero Resources' drilling activity and throughput volumes.
